scope: Proposition 10.3 (Triangular width bounds) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 80. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The choices above can be made with fixed polynomial logarithmic bounds. They give, in one round, Qout j ≤ qj + Pj(p, d∗, q>j). (10.2) where Pj is a fixed polynomial independent of qj and of all lower width logs. The total root logarithmic slice loss and the sufficient root log-side cutoff are polynomial in p, d∗ and all incoming width logs. For the interval run of Ok(1 + p) rounds in Proposition 10.2, starting without slots and with trivial width data, these width logs and the sums of root costs are polynomial in 2 + p.
